errors.text: The proposed temperature and strain-rate regime (25–900 °C and 10^-4–10^-1 s^-1) does not reconstruct the target molecular-dynamics regime of 10–600 K and 10^8–10^10 s^-1.

The hypothesis predicts room-temperature strain-rate sensitivity and high-temperature insensitivity, whereas the target result is negligible yield-strength sensitivity across 10^8–10^10 s^-1 at the simulated temperatures.

It assigns central roles to deformation twinning and FCC-to-HCP TRIP, while the target found Shockley-partial glide and stacking-fault-induced local HCP signatures without twinning or bulk phase transformation.
It replaces the defect-controlled single-crystal model with an unspecified processed material potentially containing precipitates, grain structures, and pre-existing dislocation networks.

The cited evidence does not establish the central strain-rate claim; most studies use only one strain rate, and several concern a quinary alloy, nanowires, refractory microlattices, compression, or pressure-induced transformation.
